items.title: FPI G-Sec outflows nearly halve to Rs 5,400 crore in October
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors reduced their selling of Indian government securities and equities in October compared to September. Despite this, high oil prices and global yields pose challenges for sustained portfolio inflows. Economists caution that the slowdown may not indicate a definitive change in foreign investment trends. Political dynamics in other emerging markets might influence foreign capital movement toward India.

items.title: Could Einstein's equations explain cosmic expansion without dark energy?
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

items.description: In the year 1913, the US Postal Service unveiled Parcel Post, permitting the mailing of bigger packages. Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Chester Zoo recently received National Plant Collection status for its impressive collection of Dracula orchids. These unique flowers, which mimic various shapes, face threats from habitat loss and illegal collection. Pollination occurs through specific fungi-attracting smells rather than traditional scents. Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plan…

items.title: Florida plans 4,800-acre wetlands to filter phosphorus from river water
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Florida is planning a 4,800-acre wetland project to filter phosphorus pollution before it reaches Lake Okeechobee. This initiative involves directing stormwater through treatment areas filled with aquatic vegetation. Wetlands help mitigate impacts of excess nutrients and support local ecosystems. The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

items.title: Pompeii cupboard reveals 38 bronze coins and childhood charms
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Italian archaeologists recently uncovered a sealed wooden cupboard in Pompeii, revealing artifacts from 2,000 years ago. Among the findings were 38 bronze coins, personal care items, and a unique childhood necklace. The discovery adds to our understanding of daily life in ancient Rome, highlighting ordinary people's lives. It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

items.title: 'Please listen now': Yousuf's blunt advice to Babar Azam amid batting slump
items.author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
items.description: Mohammad Yousuf has urged Babar Azam to pursue specialised coaching in Australia or South Africa. Yousuf expressed concerns over Babar's current batting struggles during the recent tri-series final against Sri Lanka. Despite Pakistan's victory, Babar's lack of significant contributions has raised questions about his form. Calls for Babar to focus on improvement before the upcoming Test series have also been voiced.
